objective: Take up backlog B92 (G1) at the coordinator's assignment on 2026-11-10, a challenge of assumption A51 (places and their neighbours are given before the rules): make the board part of the allowed states. Names are the reduced words in x, y and their inverses; an identity distinction e(u, v) for each pair of names says whether they are one place, under relation-free board axioms (transitivity, letter closure e(u, v) -> e(ug, vg), and constancy e(u, v) -> (s(u) <-> s(v))), with one uniform value law on each place and its four neighbours. Which boards do the rules allow or force? Ticket A proves what holds for every law that names no relation; ticket B runs a frozen exact census of the 1,024 Life-like one-bit laws and the atom.
stop_rule: Stop with every frozen prediction of ticket B decided and ticket A's theorems proved or their failure recorded: a clean obstruction (no law that names no relation forces an infinite board without allowing the tree, and no law of the census forces a two-dimensional board), or a law whose allowed boards are all two-dimensional, a plane chosen by the rules.
title: The board as distinctions
